phases.message: I'm Odalys, payroll and HR at Kestrelwick Software. Start in Crewmarrow: read the people on the roster and the whole change log.
Postwren is my mail. Read it. Don't reply to anyone and don't accept any offer.
Payroll Harbor runs our payroll. Read its rule and the calendar of runs through 13 November, the state accounts we already hold, and who is paid for work in which state.

Taxline State is where we open state withholding accounts. Read what each state it covers says, then register a withholding account, by person id and state, for each person whose wages need one before a run on Payroll Harbor's calendar. A state where we already hold an account needs nothing more.

Rollmark State is where we open state unemployment accounts. Read what it says, then register an unemployment account, by person id and state, for each person whose wages need one before a run on the calendar. Then tell me, for each registration, who it was for, the state and the date its run closes, and what you left alone and why.

wh_rules.text: Today is Friday 9 October 2026. Taxline State opens a state income tax withholding account for an employer. Kestrelwick Software of Portland, Oregon, pays people who work in several states. This desk covers Colorado, Minnesota, Texas and Washington; topics: general, colorado, minnesota, texas, washington. Paid leave, local and city taxes are other accounts and are not part of this chore.

- A state's withholding account is opened only where the state taxes wages.
- The state of the work taxes a nonresident's wages for work done in it.
- A state may also tax its residents wherever they work, as Colorado and Minnesota do.
- Some pairs of states have a reciprocal agreement that moves withholding to the home state; none applies to anyone on Kestrelwick's roster.
- A contractor paid on an invoice is not paid wages, and no tax is withheld.
- A state in which Kestrelwick already holds an account needs no second one.

Colorado (Department of Revenue, Wage Withholding Tax Guide, revised January 2026): every employer paying Colorado wages must withhold and 'must apply for and maintain an active Colorado wage withholding account'; the guide names no date. Colorado wages are wages paid to a Colorado resident, and wages paid to a nonresident for services performed in Colorado. There is no fee.

- Minnesota (Minn. Stat. 290.92, 2025 statutes): an employee is a resident performing services anywhere, or a nonresident performing services in Minnesota (subd. 1).
- Every employer paying wages withholds (subd. 2a).
- An employer 'shall file with the commissioner an application for a withholding account number on or before the date the employer is required to withhold Minnesota taxes' (subd. 24).
- There is no fee.
Texas: the Constitution, art. VIII, sec. 24-a, says 'The legislature may not impose a tax on the net incomes of individuals.' Texas taxes no wages, so there is no Texas withholding account to open.

Washington (Department of Revenue): 'Washington does not currently have an individual income tax.' A 9.9 percent tax on adjusted gross income over 1 million dollars begins on 1 January 2028; nothing is withheld from wages in 2026, and there is no Washington withholding account for wages.

ui_rules.text: Today is Friday 9 October 2026. Rollmark State opens a state unemployment insurance (UI) tax account for an employer. UI covers a worker's wages in one state only; topics: where, colorado, minnesota, texas, washington. Paid family leave premiums and other payroll programs are other accounts and are not part of this chore. Kestrelwick Software of Portland, Oregon, holds an Oregon account.

Colorado (C.R.S. 8-70-113 and 8-70-117, current through fall 2025): an employer is a unit that paid wages of $1,500 or more in a calendar quarter, or had a worker on some part of a day in each of 20 different weeks, in the current or preceding year. Service is employment in Colorado when it is localized there, as in the order under 'where'. The pages name no registration date.

- Minnesota (Minn. Stat. 268.035, 268.044 and 268.045, 2025 statutes): an employer is anyone who has had one or more employees in the current or prior year (268.035 subd. 14).
- An employee's whole employment in a quarter is covered if 50 percent or more of it is performed in Minnesota (subd. 12).
- An employer 'must, upon or before the submission of its first wage detail report', register for a tax account (268.045 subd. 1).
- The report is due on the last day of the month after the quarter (268.044).

Texas (Labor Code 201.021 and 201.043, verified 26 May 2025): an employer is a unit that paid wages of $1,500 or more in a calendar quarter, or had a worker in 20 or more different calendar weeks, in the current or preceding year. Service is employment in Texas when it is localized there: done entirely in Texas, or elsewhere only incidentally.

Washington (RCW 50.04.080, 50.04.110 and 50.04.120): an employer is anyone 'having any person in employment', with no wage or week minimum. Service is localized in a state if it is performed entirely there, or what is done outside it is incidental to the service within it, as when it is temporary or transitory or consists of isolated transactions.
